points.t: A waxy, warty, stuck-on brown or tan papule or plaque on the trunk or face in an adult, often many.
Benign proliferation of epidermal keratinocytes (FGFR3/PIK3CA mutations); not related to sun or HPV.
Diagnose clinically and with dermoscopy; reassure; cryotherapy or curettage only if symptomatic (often not NHS-funded for cosmetic reasons).
Melanoma that looks like an SK, irritated SK mistaken for SCC, sudden eruption of many SKs (Leser–Trélat).

points: "Stuck-on", waxy, verrucous, fissured papules and plaques, tan to black, on the trunk, face and scalp.
**Irritated SK:** red rim, crust and itch. This mimics SCC or melanoma.

cards.name: Melanoma (SSM, nodular)
cards.clue: Evolving asymmetry, atypical network, blue-white veil, irregular streaks/dots; no milia-like cysts or comedo openings. **"Ugly duckling"** among many SKs

cards.name: Clear cell acanthoma (see Clear cell acanthoma)

items.t: An ‘SK’ that is changing, has atypical dermoscopy or stands out from the patient’s other SKs: refer as a **possible melanoma**.
Sudden eruption of many SKs with itch: consider internal malignancy (**Leser–Trélat**).

pearls.t: [Case 3](condition:seborrhoeic-keratosis) sailor has lifelong UV exposure, so he is at higher risk for melanoma, BCC and SCC. Give sun-protection advice and do a **full skin check** (other lesions, scalp, ears).
Teach the "ugly duckling" concept and ask about change using photos (patients can photograph lesions monthly).
Ask about drugs that cause melanonychia (hydroxycarbamide, zidovudine, minocycline, antimalarials, cytotoxics). Multiple nails and a matching start date make it drug-related.
